daily_reality.summary: Radiologic technologists perform diagnostic imaging examinations including X-rays, CT scans, fluoroscopy, and mammography. They position patients, operate imaging equipment, ensure image quality, and follow radiation safety protocols in hospitals, outpatient centers, and physician offices.
typical_tasks: Position patients for X-ray, CT, and fluoroscopy examinations
Operate radiographic and CT equipment to produce diagnostic images
Adjust equipment settings based on patient size, anatomy, and clinical indication
Evaluate image quality and repeat if necessary
Follow radiation safety protocols including ALARA principles
Administer contrast media for CT and fluoroscopy studies
Maintain patient records and image documentation in PACS
Perform daily quality control checks on equipment
Assist radiologists during fluoroscopic and interventional procedures
Monitor patients for adverse reactions to contrast

deadlines.daily_qa: Equipment QC before first patient each morning
deadlines.routine_exams: Images available within 1-2 hours for reading
deadlines.arrt_renewal: Annual with biennial CE (24 credits/2 years)
deadlines.dose_tracking: ACR Dose Index Registry submissions per policy

daily_reality.seasonality: ER imaging increases with seasonal accidents, sports injuries, and flu-related complications. Screening mammography campaigns may create seasonal peaks. Otherwise relatively steady year-round.

regulatory.summary: ARRT certification required in most states. State licensure required in majority of states. Must complete JRCERT-accredited program. Radiation dose monitoring and safety regulations under state and federal law.

key_laws.name: Mammography Quality Standards Act (MQSA)
key_laws.detail: FDA regulation requiring certification of mammography facilities and qualified personnel

key_laws.name: State Radiation Control Programs
key_laws.detail: State licensing and inspection of radiographic equipment and personnel

key_laws.name: 10 CFR Part 20
key_laws.detail: NRC radiation protection standards (for facilities with NRC-regulated sources)

key_laws.name: HIPAA
key_laws.detail: Patient imaging data and PHI protection

requirements: ARRT R.T.(R) certification — Registered Technologist in Radiography
State licensure required in most states
24 CE credits every 2 years for ARRT renewal
Advanced certifications available: CT, mammography, fluoroscopy, bone densitometry
certifying_bodies: ARRT — American Registry of Radiologic Technologists
JRCERT — Joint Review Committee on Education in Radiologic Technology

regulatory.penalties: State can revoke license for unsafe practices. MQSA violations can shut down mammography facilities. ARRT certification loss for ethical violations. Facilities cited for radiation safety violations.

tools.summary: Radiologic technologists operate X-ray, CT, fluoroscopy, and mammography equipment from manufacturers like GE, Siemens, Philips, and Canon. PACS systems store and distribute images. AI-assisted tools increasingly used for image quality and dose optimization.

primary_software.name: CT scanners (GE Revolution, Siemens SOMATOM, Philips Incisive)
Digital fluoroscopy systems
primary_software.purpose: Real-time X-ray imaging for GI, cardiac, interventional procedures

primary_software.name: PACS (Sectra, GE Centricity, Philips IntelliSpace)
primary_software.purpose: Picture Archiving and Communication System for image storage

pain_points: Keeping up with rapidly evolving CT technology

terminology.summary: Radiologic technologists use medical imaging, radiation physics, and anatomy terminology covering positioning, exposure parameters, and image quality.

key_terms.meaning: Kilovoltage Peak — controls X-ray beam penetration
Milliampere-seconds — controls X-ray beam quantity (radiation dose)
As Low As Reasonably Achievable — radiation safety principle
Computed Radiography / Digital Radiography — digital X-ray systems
Restricting X-ray beam to area of interest to reduce dose
Injected/ingested agents to enhance visibility of structures
CT Dose Index — measure of radiation dose per CT scan
Dose Length Product — total radiation dose for CT examination
Unwanted image degradation from motion, metal, or technique
Image display settings for viewing different tissue types
Mobile fluoroscopy unit for OR and bedside procedures

career_psychology.summary: Radiologic technologists have a clear certification advancement path with specialty credentials (CT, MRI, mammography). Median salary $77,660 with good growth outlook. Physical demands and radiation exposure are ongoing concerns.

career_levels.responsibilities: General X-ray, portable imaging, fluoroscopy assistance
CT scanning, contrast administration, complex positioning
Department management, protocol development, equipment procurement

main_fears: Imaging wrong body part or wrong patient
burnout_causes: Physical demands of positioning patients and moving portable equipment
High patient volume in busy ER departments
growth_motivation: Advanced ARRT credentials (CT, MRI, mammography, interventional)
Medical dosimetry or radiology PA pathway

market.summary: Median salary $77,660 (BLS May 2024). 5% growth projected 2024-2034 with ~15,400 annual openings. About 235,200 employed. One of the largest medical imaging professions.
market.job_outlook: 5% growth 2024-2034, faster than average. ~15,400 annual openings.

work_arrangements.dominant: W-2 employees at hospitals (55%+), outpatient imaging centers, physician offices
work_arrangements.travel: Travel RT positions with premium pay through staffing agencies
work_arrangements.shift_patterns: Evenings, weekends, and overnight shifts common, especially in hospitals

market_trends: AI-assisted image interpretation and quality optimization
Portable/mobile imaging growing in ambulatory settings
Dual-energy CT and spectral imaging creating advanced skill requirements
Dose reduction technology reducing cumulative technologist exposure
